UnitStatement: `dbm-section-publish` defines the INIT-TASK dispatch contract for `TASK + dbm-section-publish`.
Use `dbm-section-publish` when DBM_PUBLISHER needs one approved DBM section synthesized from frozen publication planning artifacts and exact mapped KTY-local inputs.
`ScopePath` should normally be the section-local publication folder `{EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Publication/DBM/sections/{SECTION_ID}/`.
`AllowedWriteTargets` must name exactly the section body markdown and the section QA markdown.
A `dbm-section-publish` brief must not grant broader publication-root or KTY-folder write access.
Required brief-level fields include `PURPOSE`, `ScopePath`, `TaskSkill`, `AllowedWriteTargets`, and `ExpectedOutputs`.
Required runtime overrides include section identity, section metadata, two output paths, the publication manifest, schema, section map, rules, and `MAX_KA_FILES`.
`DBM_OUTPUT_MODE` defaults to full engineering DBM when omitted.
`SECTION_CONTEXT_PATH` identifies a deterministic per-section structural context packet.
`OPEN_ITEM_PACKET` carries section-relevant unresolved human rulings, engineering TBDs, and decomposition/publication gaps from DBM_PUBLISHER mapped-KTY scanning.
`ALLOW_CONTEXT_ONLY_DECOMP_FALLBACK` controls whether decomposition fallback is allowed for unready `CONTEXT_ONLY` inputs.
A supersession map may be supplied with root and facility identifiers for applicability filtering.
Hypergraph runtime fields may admit a use mode, snapshot, nodes, hyperedges, and evidence root.
`SECTION_TYPE` must match the approved section taxonomy in `Publication_Schema.md`.
`SECTION_OUTPUT_PATH` and `SECTION_QA_OUTPUT_PATH` must both live inside `ScopePath`.
`MAX_KA_FILES` should match the approved section design rather than an ad hoc worker preference.
The section worker should receive only planning artifacts and mapped inputs already frozen for the run.
`SECTION_CONTEXT_PATH` is read-only structural context and does not replace mapped KA content as body-authoring authority.
`OPEN_ITEM_PACKET` is operational caveat context and does not expand body-authoring authority or permit unmapped content.
`DBM_DIGEST` must be explicit in the brief and publication rules when selected by the human.
A full engineering DBM brief should include completeness standards, expected body components, table/data expectations, geometry treatment, and section adequacy risks.
When a supersession map is admitted, `ROOT_NAME` and `FACILITY_ID` should make applicability filtering unambiguous against the manifest facility.
`CustomInstructions` should be limited to run-specific reinforcement.
`CustomInstructions` must not recreate the skill contract because TASK hydration loads the authoritative contract.
A valid `dbm-section-publish` run requires both required outputs: the section body markdown and the section QA markdown.
The section body must read as coherent engineering prose under `Publication_Rules.md` rather than as a concatenated artifact dump.
The section body must reflect current post-SCA state when mapped sources require a state choice.
Unsupported claims must be surfaced as `TBD`, assumptions, or conflicts rather than silently guessed.
Detailed inline source citations must not appear in the section body; detailed provenance belongs in QA and the package trace appendix.
The section QA artifact must use the required stable block structure in the required order.
All writes must stay inside the approved section-local publication folder.
When `SECTION_CONTEXT_PATH` is provided, section QA must record whether structural context was consumed.
When `SECTION_CONTEXT_PATH` is provided, section QA must flag any mapped `PRIMARY` KTY with no material body contribution.
Body prose may use only reader-facing epistemic labels, while original governance-state labels remain in QA.
In `FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM` mode, the body must be usable for core engineering design basis without reopening KA files.
In `FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM` mode, DBM-native engineering structure must be used instead of mapped assertions, raw caveat dumps, file inventories, or trace scaffolds.
Design-basis tables must be included, consolidated, split, or explicitly omitted/deferred with rationale.
Trace-only treatment must not be used for body-worthy design-basis tables.
`PRIMARY` KTYs with multiple material facts, tables, or open requirements must not be collapsed to token mentions or one generic sentence.
`QA_CHECKS.md` lists ten required section QA H2 headings in a fixed order.
Notes: Potential internal conflict: SKILL.md later adds Assertion Emission Notes and conditional Auxiliary Structure Warnings.

UnitStatement: `Coverage Table` records mapped KTYs and KAs consumed, plus mapped inputs skipped and the skip reason.
`Coverage Table` must identify materially contributing `PRIMARY` KTYs and `PRIMARY` KTYs with zero visible body contribution.
`Design Basis Content Coverage` records applicable content classes as `INCLUDED`, `OMITTED_WITH_RATIONALE`, `DEFERRED_UPSTREAM_MISSING`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE`.
`Table Treatment` records design-basis table handling with the controlled statuses listed by the QA checks.
`Section Adequacy Findings` records fixed finding codes when present.
`Readiness Observations` records KTY readiness issues.
`Conflict Register` records contradictory values or states and both mapped positions.
`Gap / TBD Register` preserves distinctions among human authority rulings, TBDs, assumptions, deferred confirmations, external responsibility, and decomposition/publication gaps.
Use `FAILED_INPUTS` when required runtime overrides are missing.
Use `FAILED_INPUTS` when mapped `PRIMARY` or `CONFLICTING` inputs are below readiness threshold.
Use `FAILED_INPUTS` when the section input set exceeds `MAX_KA_FILES` or the approved size limit.
Use `FAILED_INPUTS` when output paths fall outside the approved section-local publication folder.
Use `FAILED` when a required output cannot be written despite valid inputs.
Use `FAILED` when an internal run error prevents stable outputs from being emitted.
Even non-blocking runs must surface skipped supporting inputs, terminology normalizations, remaining conflicts, and remaining TBDs or assumptions in QA.
Even non-blocking runs must surface amendment reliance, supersession body notes, context-packet factual-use overrides, content-adequacy findings, and table treatment decisions in QA.
`dbm-section-publish` publishes exactly one rewritten DBM section from approved mapped DOMAIN inputs and emits fixed QA artifacts.
The skill consumes frozen publication planning artifacts and reads only mapped KTY-local inputs for its assigned section.
The skill emits one section body and one section QA artifact.
`dbm-section-publish` is the primary publication authoring unit in v1.
`dbm-section-publish` is not a dispatcher and does not redesign the publication schema or section map.
`dbm-section-publish` runs in the generic TASK shell with no profile.
The typical dispatcher is DBM_PUBLISHER after human approval of frozen planning artifacts.
The skill requires section identity, title, type, purpose, output paths, publication planning paths, and `MAX_KA_FILES`.
Optional runtime overrides include output mode, source domain, section order, context path, open item packet, context fallback, and hypergraph inputs.
`SECTION_TYPE` is limited to `OVERVIEW`, `PROCESS_BASIS`, `PHILOSOPHY`, `DATA_REFERENCE`, `DISCIPLINE_BASIS`, or `REGULATORY`.
`SECTION_OUTPUT_PATH` and `SECTION_QA_OUTPUT_PATH` are required paths under `_Publication/DBM/sections/{SECTION_ID}/`.
The `SUPERSESSION_MAP_PATH` applies blank `AppliesToSections` globally and nonblank `AppliesToSections` only when it includes the current `SECTION_ID`.
The skill is reasoning-first and consumes deterministic planning artifacts produced outside the skill.
The `allowed-tools` frontmatter field is omitted because the skill has no deterministic tool requirements of its own.
The skill must not dispatch other tasks.
The skill must not write outside the four section output paths.
Notes: Potential internal inconsistency: surrounding source material defines exactly two section outputs.

UnitStatement: The skill must not modify any `CAT-* / 1_Working / KTY-*` files.
The skill must not perform guessed discovery outside frozen planning artifacts and approved section-map rows.
The skill must not use `_MEMORY.md` or `_SEMANTIC.md` as factual authority.
When the skill reads a mapped KTY `_STATUS.md`, it must also read sibling `_MEMORY.md` as non-authoritative operational context.
Admitted hypergraph evidence is read-only for local QA checks and must not drive section body synthesis.
The skill must not convert unresolved rulings, TBDs, assumptions, deferred confirmations, or gaps into confirmed design claims.
In `FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM` mode, raw caveat dumps, file-path inventories, and trace scaffolds must not stand in as the main body structure.
`SECTION_OUTPUT_PATH` is the rewritten DBM section body output.
`SECTION_QA_OUTPUT_PATH` is the stable section QA artifact output.
The authority hierarchy starts with approved `Publication_Schema.md`.
Approved `Publication_Rules.md` and approved `Section_Map.csv` follow the publication schema in the authority hierarchy.
The frozen `Publication_Input_Manifest.md` follows the approved schema, rules, and section map in the authority hierarchy.
The section context packet, when provided, is structural context for framing and completeness checks only.
Accepted scope-change state and approved decomposition state named in the manifest are authority inputs.
Exact mapped KTY-local files named in the section map are authority inputs below the planning and accepted-state artifacts.
Vocabulary maps, decision logs, and open-issues registers named in the manifest are consulted when required by mapped rows or QA work.
Original/reference markdown and provenance tables do not override accepted DOMAIN/SCA state or mapped CAT/KTY/KA-local content.
`FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM` is the default DBM output mode.
In `FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM`, the section body must be a DBM-native engineering section, not a digest or current-state summary.
In `FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM`, the body must carry core design basis without requiring readers to reopen KA files.
`DBM_DIGEST` is allowed only when the dispatch brief or frozen publication rules explicitly select it.
When digest mode is used, section QA must state it and must not present the output as a full governing DBM section.
`OPEN_ITEM_PACKET` is operational caveat context and does not authorize new body claims or expand the mapped input set.
Section-relevant human authority rulings must be surfaced in QA and, when they affect current design basis, in the body as unresolved decisions.
Engineering uncertainty should be written as explicit `TBD`, `to be confirmed`, or `assumed` statements in body prose when body treatment is needed.
Original labels such as `TBD`, `ASSUMPTION`, `DEFERRED_CONFIRMATION`, `ExternalResponsibility`, and human-ruling status must be preserved in section QA.
Decomposition and publication gaps must be identified as limitations or follow-up requirements, not as content to invent.
Retired, tombstoned, archived-stubbed, or no-factual-use KTYs are non-authoring inputs unless the section map and rules explicitly allow context-only treatment.
The skill must preserve accepted SCA supersession state without inferring additional supersessions from prose.
Hypergraph evidence is read-only auxiliary structure evidence for section workers.
Hypergraph evidence does not enter the content authority stack for section body synthesis.
When hypergraph evidence is admitted, it may be used only for local QA checks about omitted connected support or cross-section consistency.
Hypergraph evidence must not author or rewrite section body prose.
Hypergraph evidence must not override mapped CAT/KTY/KA-local content.
Hypergraph evidence must not contradict the approved section map or decomposition mappings.
Hypergraph-derived QA concerns must be labeled `AUXILIARY_STRUCTURE_WARNING` in section QA.
The section worker must not block its own output on hypergraph QA findings.
`PRIMARY` mapped material anchors section narrative and structure.
`SUPPORTING` mapped material informs the section contextually or constrainingly but does not define primary structure.
`CONFLICTING` mapped input is known to contradict other mapped inputs and must be surfaced without silent reconciliation.
`CONTEXT_ONLY` mapped material is background-only and should not drive direct design-basis claims unless publication rules explicitly permit it.
`FULL_ARTIFACT` means the whole artifact may contribute.
`TARGET_HEADING` means only the heading or subsection named in section-map notes may contribute.
`TABLE_ONLY` means only tabular content may contribute.
`VALUES_ONLY` means only explicit values and parameters may contribute.
`BACKGROUND_ONLY` means background context only and forbids direct design-basis claims.
An `OVERVIEW` section template covers facility identity, objectives, scope boundaries, key assumptions or constraints, and document applicability.
For `OVERVIEW` sections, structural context from `SECTION_CONTEXT_PATH` may become body-authoring authority for facility-level framing.
The `OVERVIEW` structural-context authority expansion is limited to facility and document framing.
The `OVERVIEW` structural-context authority expansion does not permit inventing technical values, equipment requirements, operating conditions, capacities, limits, or product specifications.
A `PROCESS_BASIS` section template covers purpose, functional configuration, design/operating basis, interfaces, controls/protection, and facility-specific notes.
A `PHILOSOPHY` section template covers governing principle, applicability, required design behavior, exceptions or limits, and rationale.
A `DATA_REFERENCE` section template covers narrative introduction, consolidated values or tables, assumptions or caveats, and usage notes.
A `DISCIPLINE_BASIS` section template covers discipline scope, governing basis, required systems/components, constraints/standards, and interfaces.
A `REGULATORY` section template covers governing obligation, applicability, facility impact, compliance implications, and unresolved items.
In `FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM` mode, default templates are minimum outlines only.
The worker must assess mapped active material against design-basis content classes and include every applicable class or explain omissions in section QA.
Design-basis content classes include governing criteria, design values, equipment configuration, operating cases, protections, standards, interfaces, assumptions, and tabular data.
If approved section design cannot carry applicable material without collapsing systems, tables, or design cases into a digest, emit `UNDERDEVELOPED_SECTION` in section QA.
When `UNDERDEVELOPED_SECTION` is emitted, section QA must explain the required split or schema repair.
Design-basis tables in mapped material must be preserved, consolidated, split, or reconstructed as equivalent body tables when they contain material engineering values.
A worker must not omit material design-basis tables merely because detailed provenance has moved to the trace appendix.
Allowed table treatments are `INCLUDED`, `CONSOLIDATED`, `SPLIT`, `OMITTED_WITH_RATIONALE`, `TRACE_ONLY`, `DEFERRED_UPSTREAM_MISSING`, and `NONE_APPLICABLE`.
`TRACE_ONLY` table treatment is valid only for trace, index, provenance, reference-list, or non-design-basis tables.
Omitting a design-basis table without rationale is an `UNJUSTIFIED_TABLE_OMISSION` finding.
The frozen `Publication_Input_Manifest.md` is the primary freshness boundary for the run.
Before reading mapped KTY-local files, the skill must confirm manifest-recorded publication admission for the root.
Root publication admission evidence includes active root handoff state, publication-admission or closure evidence, and non-blocking audit evidence.
If publication admission evidence is missing or records the root as not publication-admissible, the skill fails with `FAILED_INPUTS`.
After root publication admission passes, the skill must read each mapped KTY `_STATUS.md` before using its files.
Whenever mapped KTY `_STATUS.md` is read, sibling `_MEMORY.md` must also be read as non-authoritative operational context.
`PRIMARY` and `CONFLICTING` inputs must be at least `INITIALIZED`.
A `PRIMARY` input below readiness threshold causes `FAILED_INPUTS`.
A `CONFLICTING` input below readiness threshold causes `FAILED_INPUTS`.
A `SUPPORTING` input below readiness threshold is skipped and recorded as a gap note in section QA.
A below-threshold `CONTEXT_ONLY` input may fall back to decomposition-level context only when `ALLOW_CONTEXT_ONLY_DECOMP_FALLBACK=true`, with a QA note.
A material disagreement between manifest/root publication-admission evidence and local `_STATUS.md` causes `FAILED_INPUTS` and a QA mismatch record.
Local `_STATUS.md` files are not sufficient publication admission evidence on their own.
An `OPEN` or otherwise unready KTY must not be treated as equivalent to a fully authored KTY artifact.
When the manifest provides a vocabulary map, the skill should prefer canonical terms over KA-local synonyms.
A synonym should be retained in parentheses only when it materially helps recognition.
The section should avoid mixed terminology for the same system.
If multiple mapped artifacts agree, the skill synthesizes them into one coherent narrative.
If mapped artifacts differ, the skill must not reconcile them silently.
For differing artifacts, supersession row eligibility requires root and facility match; blank `AppliesToSections` is global and populated `AppliesToSections` must include the current section.
An eligible `SUPERSESSION` binding requires applying the replacement value and recording the binding reference in section QA.
An eligible `SUPPLEMENTARY_EXTENSION` binding preserves accepted current-state basis and records supplementary detail in QA or trace when relevant.
Unresolved contradictions between mapped content and admitted reference/provenance material must be recorded in QA rather than silently resolved.
Publication conflicts without an accepted resolution should be recorded in section QA and handled with cautious narrative wording.
If a system exists in only one facility or domain, the section must scope that system explicitly to that facility.
If a system moved between facilities due to accepted SCA, the body presents the post-SCA arrangement as current state and keeps prior placement as audit context only.
If content is absent for a facility, the skill must not invent parity and should use `TBD` or an explicit scope note.
By default, supersession history appears in section QA and `Trace_Appendix.md`, not in section body prose.
A body supersession note is allowed only when supersession affects a current design-basis value or scope state stated in the body.
A body supersession note is allowed only when the superseded value or state is likely to remain visible in admitted or legacy references.
A body supersession note is allowed only when omitting it could cause a reader to treat the current value as an error.
A body supersession note must be concise engineering prose without governance process history.
Process-history supersession notes should not be written in body prose.
When in doubt, supersession body notes should be omitted and the amendment context recorded in section QA.
Every substantive claim must be supported by mapped CAT/KTY/KA-local artifacts or approved planning artifacts.
Unsupported statements become `TBD`.
Uncertain synthesis becomes an exposed conflict or an explicitly labeled assumption.
Inline `[HBK-####]`-style citations are not allowed in the DBM body.
Detailed traceability belongs in the trace appendix and section QA outputs.
Body prose normalizes unresolved states to reader-appropriate labels: `TBD`, `to be confirmed`, or `assumed`.
Governance-state labels such as `DEFERRED`, `BLOCKED`, `PENDING`, or `DEFERRED_CONFIRMATION` must not appear in body prose.
Original governance-state labels must be preserved in section QA.
Every `PRIMARY` mapped KTY should contribute all material applicable facts, tables, constraints, interfaces, assumptions, and TBDs unless QA records a clear exception.
One sentence per `PRIMARY` KTY is insufficient when the KTY contains multiple material facts, tables, operating cases, equipment details, or open requirements.
If a material `PRIMARY` KTY is collapsed to a token mention or generic sentence, section QA must emit `PRIMARY_KTY_COLLAPSED`.
`SUPPORTING` artifacts qualify, constrain, or trace claims anchored by `PRIMARY` artifacts.
`SUPPORTING` artifacts should not create standalone claims unless the section map or publication rules assign that role.
`CONTEXT_ONLY` artifacts do not produce body claims.
`CONTEXT_ONLY` artifacts may shape QA, trace, framing checks, or explicit scope exclusions.
The skill fails fast with `FAILED_INPUTS` if mapped KA count exceeds `MAX_KA_FILES`.
The skill fails fast with `FAILED_INPUTS` if the section input set exceeds approved size rules.
When section inputs are oversized, DBM_PUBLISHER must split or refine the section design rather than force oversized synthesis.
The method starts by validating inputs and write boundary.
The method requires reading frozen planning artifacts and confirming root publication admission.
The section context packet is structural context and not a substitute for mapped KA content.
The section context packet may be used to understand why mapped KTYs matter and to verify completeness.
If a mapped KTY has `FACTUAL_USE_GATE = BLOCK_FACTUAL_USE`, the worker must treat it as `CONTEXT_ONLY` and record the override in QA.
The section context packet may be used to identify applicable supersession bindings and open issues before body drafting.
The open-item packet determines section-relevant human rulings, engineering TBDs, and decomposition/publication gaps.
Open-item packet items must be preserved in QA even when body prose flattens them for readability.
For each mapped KTY, the worker reads only listed mapped publication inputs.
Mapped publication inputs include `Scoping.md`, mapped `KA-*.md`, `_CONTEXT.md`, `_REFERENCES.md`, `_STATUS.md`, and paired `_MEMORY.md`.
Optional `_DEPENDENCIES.md` is read only when explicitly required by the section map or publication rules.
The worker applies root admission, readiness gates, selector semantics, KTY readiness, and publication-rule precedence before drafting.
The worker drafts the section body according to section type, publication rules, output mode, completeness standard, body components, and table treatment expectations.
In `FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM` mode, body drafting uses DBM-native engineering headings and subsections rather than QA or export artifact structures.
Before finalizing QA, the worker assesses standalone design-basis adequacy, DBM-native structure, content coverage, table treatment, and `PRIMARY` KTY use.
The worker emits stable section QA using the fixed structure.
The worker returns status conservatively, using `FAILED_INPUTS` for invalid or oversized inputs and otherwise surfacing gaps and conflicts.
`SKILL.md` requires section QA to contain fixed blocks through `Assertion Emission Notes`, plus conditional `Auxiliary Structure Warnings` when hypergraph evidence is consumed.
Notes: Potential internal conflict: QA_CHECKS.md lists ten required QA headings without Assertion Emission Notes or Auxiliary Structure Warnings.

UnitStatement: Section QA must preserve distinctions such as `TBD`, `ASSUMPTION`, and `DEFERRED_CONFIRMATION` even when body prose flattens unresolved items.
`Design Basis Content Coverage` in section QA records each applicable content class with controlled inclusion or omission statuses and concise rationale.
`Table Treatment` in section QA must not use `TRACE_ONLY` for body-worthy design-basis tables.

`Section Adequacy Findings` records fixed codes including `UNDERDEVELOPED_SECTION`, `UNJUSTIFIED_TABLE_OMISSION`, `PRIMARY_KTY_COLLAPSED`, `MISSING_DESIGN_BASIS_CLASS`, `QA_SCAFFOLD_BODY_LEAKAGE`, and `NON_STANDALONE_CORE_BASIS`.
The tool policy preferred order is to read frozen planning artifacts before context packets and mapped KTY-local files.
The tool policy uses direct reasoning to synthesize the section body and QA artifact after reading permitted inputs.
TASK-enforced deterministic tools are none for `dbm-section-publish`.
Operational deterministic tools are none for `dbm-section-publish`.
The reasoning role includes interpreting mapped inputs under `MappingRole` and `ContributionScope`.
The reasoning role uses section context packets without promoting them to body-authoring authority except for the narrow `OVERVIEW` framing exception.
The reasoning role applies publication-rule precedence and synthesizes coherent engineering prose.
In `FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM` mode, reasoning must preserve material engineering detail and design-basis tables in DBM-native body structure.
Reasoning must preserve uncertainty as `TBD`, assumptions, or conflicts rather than inventing reconciliations.
The skill must not use `_Aggregation/*`, `_Coordination/*`, `_Evaluation/*`, `_Reconciliation/*`, `_MEMORY.md`, or `_SEMANTIC.md` as content authority.
The skill must not perform package-level assembly.
The skill must not use QA/export scaffolds as the default body structure in `FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM` mode.
The tool policy write boundary allows only one section body markdown file and one section QA markdown file.
All writes must remain inside the section-local publication folder named in the INIT-TASK brief.
